record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.original_question: In preferential attachment models that allow vertex and/or edge removal, rather than pure growth where added vertices and edges remain forever, how do specific removal mechanisms affect global network quantities beyond the expected degree sequence, especially the component structure, existence of a giant component, and persistence or time-variation of the vertex of maximal degree?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to analyse the effect of vertex and/or edge removal on other quantities, such as the component structure and the vertex of maximal degree.
For a given choice of removal mechanism, does the network contain a giant component? Is the vertex with maximal degree persistent, or does it change with time?

artifact.status_search_result: The general question is broadly open, but specific sub-cases have been addressed. Recent works study preferential attachment trees with vertex death, establishing both lack of persistence of the maximum degree in some regimes and persistence in others. There are also results on emergence of the giant component in preferential attachment without vertex growth and on robustness of the giant component under random edge removal. A unified picture across general removal mechanisms remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Preferential Attachment Trees with Vertex Death: Persistence of the Maximum Degree
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions for persistence of maximum degree in preferential attachment with vertex death, complementing earlier studies of lack of persistence.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist on persistence/non-persistence of the maximum degree under vertex death.

status_evidence.title: Preferential attachment trees with vertex death: lack of persistence
status_evidence.snippet: Studies preferential attachment trees with vertex death and shows lack of persistence of the maximum degree in certain regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Lack-of-persistence results are known for some vertex-death preferential attachment models.

status_evidence.title: Preferential attachment without vertex growth: emergence of the giant component
status_evidence.snippet: Studies emergence of the giant component in a preferential attachment dynamics without vertex growth.
status_evidence.claim: Giant component existence has been analyzed in specific non-growing preferential attachment models.

status_evidence.title: Random networks with sublinear preferential attachment: The giant component
status_evidence.snippet: Criteria for the existence of a giant component and robustness under random edge removal in sublinear preferential attachment.
status_evidence.claim: Edge-removal robustness of the giant component has been studied in sublinear preferential attachment.
